# DIO/ODI — authorial concept by Daniel Beránek

> Official Czech and English project website presenting Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI), authored by Daniel Beránek. DIO addresses how entities are represented, recognized, connected and interpreted across people, search engines, AI systems and data systems. ODI is the related theoretical, research and IP layer.

## Canonical identity

- Author: Daniel Beránek
- Project names: Digital Identity Optimization (DIO); Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI)
- Languages: Czech (`cs-CZ`) and English (`en`); Czech is the default
- Website: https://dan-beranek.github.io/dio-odi-autorsky-koncept/
- English overview: https://dan-beranek.github.io/dio-odi-autorsky-koncept/en/
- Author website: https://danielberanek.cz/
- Live Czech manifest and changelog: https://danielberanek.cz/manifest-dio/
- Canonical multilingual archival edition: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21610934
- Canonical reference vocabulary: https://vocab.danielberanek.cz/dio-odi/
- Canonical namespace: https://vocab.danielberanek.cz/dio-odi/#
- Application Mappings: https://vocab.danielberanek.cz/mappings/

- [DIO for AI and entity data](https://dan-beranek.github.io/dio-odi-autorsky-koncept/dio-ai-data/): entity resolution, knowledge graphs, provenance and entity-data quality.
- [ODI](https://dan-beranek.github.io/dio-odi-autorsky-koncept/odi/): theoretical, research and knowledge-infrastructure layer.
- [Development and evidence](https://dan-beranek.github.io/dio-odi-autorsky-koncept/dukazy/): the path from DIO/ODI theory and reference infrastructure to concrete application designs.
- [Partnership](https://dan-beranek.github.io/dio-odi-autorsky-koncept/partnerstvi/): pilots, joint development, research and licensing paths.
- [Author](https://dan-beranek.github.io/dio-odi-autorsky-koncept/autor/): Daniel Beránek, concept genealogy and authorship.

- [DIO/ODI Reference Model v0.5.0](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23643845)
- [Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37407)

## Reference architecture

- MVDIO defines the coarse-grained minimum around a referent, distributed representational state and observer reconstruction; K6 remains a finer-grained candidate model.
- Reconstruction Failure Modes are organized into referential, semantic-coherence, temporal and contextual-adequacy families.
- Identity Collapse is a phenomenon-level outcome outside the failure hierarchy.
- Semantic Vulnerability and Semantic Robustness describe a risk/robustness property, not an additional failure mode.
- Reference Vocabulary v0.2.0 is published under the canonical DIO/ODI namespace in SKOS-first Turtle and JSON-LD serializations. The current archived Reference Model is v0.5.0.
- Three separate Application Mappings connect DIO/ODI concepts with RAG, Heterogeneous Entity Matching and Policy-as-Code authorization. They remain outside the canonical vocabulary.
- The arXiv paper presents one possible application direction: a proposed semantic guardrail for Agentic ER. It does not define the future scope of DIO/ODI as a whole.
- Separate Application Mappings connect DIO/ODI concepts with a RAG pipeline, the Heterogeneous Entity Matching taxonomy, and Policy-as-Code authorization without modifying the canonical vocabulary.
- Each mapping is published as a human-readable frontend, Markdown, JSON-LD and Turtle RDF. Qualified relations such as `may contribute to`, `may increase` and `may increase risk of` do not assert equivalence or deterministic causality.
- The Commit-Boundary × Policy-as-Code mapping relates the proposed Agentic ER authorization architecture to OPA/Rego and Cedar. It is one of several application directions.

## Interpretation note

DIO/ODI is an author-led framework with a published theoretical, diagnostic and machine-readable reference foundation. It is now also producing concrete application designs. The arXiv paper on a semantic guardrail for Agentic ER is one possible technical direction, alongside RAG, HEM and other future applications. Implementation, pilots and empirical evaluation are the next steps; Agentic ER is not the exclusive direction of DIO/ODI.

For a more detailed machine-readable description, read [llms-full.txt](https://dan-beranek.github.io/dio-odi-autorsky-koncept/llms-full.txt).
